When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10**, WATCH vs VIX Spike tier **2/4** (MEDIUM), probability **60%**, skew and backwardation both active
The Crash Index reads price damage that has already happened. The VIX detector reads what options traders pay for protection right now. Trust the VIX read for the next few sessions, because it looks forward and the Crash Index looks back.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime state **28**, STABLE, no regime shift vs Risk-off bias with **5** signals aligned and the jaws composite at **100**
A stable score says the regime has not flipped yet. The bias and the jaws say pressure is building under it. Trust the bias for sizing, and treat the stable label as a lagging confirmation.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **64**, ACCUMULATE vs Macro regime CONTRACTION at **70%** confidence
The contrarian gauge sees a partial buy setup while the macro regime argues for patience. Trust the regime for how much you commit, and use the contrarian reading only to stage small entries.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The call is defensive with a calm surface. The Crash Index sits at 1/10 and the regime state reads stable at 28, yet the macro regime is CONTRACTION at 70% confidence and 5 risk-off signals line up. The VIX detector sits at tier 2/4 with a 60% spike probability, and both skew and backwardation are active. Price is quiet, but the options market is already paying up for protection.

That gap shapes your positioning. The contrarian score of 64 says accumulation has a partial case, which means scale in small and keep dry powder for a better price. Small caps lead the US at +2.0% over five days while the Nasdaq 100 slips -0.8%, so the strength is not coming from the crowded growth leaders. Hold hedges where they are cheap relative to the 60% spike probability, and keep gross exposure below what a CONTRACTION regime would normally support.

The main risk is a vol expansion that arrives before the Crash Index reacts, since that gauge only moves after prices fall. The divergence composite sits in the ELEVATED zone with 53% of pairs diverging, and 15 pairs lean bearish against 8 bullish. The read flips if backwardation and skew both fade while the spike tier drops back below 2/4. Then the calm price action is telling the truth and the defensive bias has been early.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The regime is CONTRACTION at 70% confidence. That confidence is firm enough to set your base stance but leaves 30% for a different reading, so avoid all in positions.

Favor quality balance sheets, shorter duration risk, and holdings that pay you while you wait. Keep cyclical exposure light until the regime score moves, since the regime state sits at 28 with no shift yet.

The contrarian reading of 64 allows partial accumulation, so buy in stages and make each stage smaller than the last. A drop in the confidence figure from 70% would open the door to adding risk.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together have started to move apart. Correlation drift is the size of that split, measured as how much their tie has changed over time.

The composite sits in the ELEVATED zone with 53% of the 43 pairs diverging, and the mother jaws score reads 100. The top six pairs all score 80.

The yield curve pair (T10Y2Y) moved from -0.42 to +0.41, and stocks against long bonds (SPY and TLT) went from +0.73 to -0.31, which means bonds no longer cushion equity drops. Regional banks against financials (KRE and XLF) flipped from +0.33 to -0.71, a stress marker inside the financial sector.

High beta against low volatility (SPHB and SPLV) fell from +0.94 to +0.38, and energy against tech (XLE and XLK) moved from -0.86 to +0.37. The net bias is 7 pairs bearish, with 15 bearish against 8 bullish.

When so many old relationships break at once, diversification works worse than it did a month ago, so size positions as if your holdings will move together on a bad day.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Asia leans weak. Hong Kong's Hang Seng lags at -5.7% over five days while Australia's ASX 200 holds at -0.1%, so the damage sits in China linked markets.

Europe splits between Switzerland at +1.4% and France at -1.6%, which shows money favoring defensive Swiss large caps over French cyclicals. The US shows a similar rotation, with the Russell 2000 up +2.0% and the Nasdaq 100 down -0.8%.

Crypto trades in a tight, soft band, with Ethereum at -1.0% and Solana at -1.3%, so there is no strong risk appetite coming from that side. For the US session, expect a market that favors small caps and defensives over mega cap tech.

A further slide in Hong Kong would weigh on the Nasdaq 100 first.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

These two gauges disagree, and the disagreement is coherent. The Crash Index at 1/10 (WATCH) measures damage in price: drawdowns, breadth breaks, credit stress.

None of that has shown up. The VIX Spike Detector at tier 2/4 (MEDIUM) with a 60% probability measures what options traders charge for insurance, and with skew and backwardation both active, near term fear costs more than fear further out.

That pattern usually appears before prices move, because hedgers buy protection first and sellers follow later. The adaptive trigger is still off, so the alarm is half raised.

Trust the VIX reading for the next few sessions and the Crash Index for confirmation. If the Crash Index climbs above 1/10 while backwardation persists, the two gauges agree and the risk is no longer a warning.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

Score 0-2 CALM · 3-4 WATCH · 5-6 WARNING · 7-8 ALARM · 9-10 EXTREME (rare crash imminent). Lead times: structural 30-90d · stress 5-30d · triggers 1-10d. Four Telegram alerts available depending on escalation.
How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

How to read

Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
